deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematical derivation on this page. It is a pencil draft ('Blatt 13; Bleistift') of Riemann's natural-philosophical and psychological fragments. Dedekind and Weber printed related texts in the Gesammelte Werke under 'Fragmente philosophischen Inhalts' ('Zur Psychologie und Metaphysik' and 'Neue mathematische Principien der Naturphilosophie'). The content restated:

(A) Left column: postulates 'to explain reproduction by memory and imagination'.
(1) Every representation (act of mental life) forms something permanent that strives to reproduce it. Marginal addition: this permanent thing does not act lastingly on the world of appearances, but shows itself under suitable conditions by reproducing the representation. Riemann calls it 'Geistesmasse' (mind-mass).
(2) Reproducing an earlier representation means that its Geistesmasse generates a like-formed Geistesmasse, which unites with it.
(3) Newly forming Geistesmassen combine to definite degrees with each other and with older ones.
(4) The soul is a compact, intimately and manifoldly interconnected Geistesmasse. It grows continually by new Geistesmassen, and this growth is its development.
(7) The form of a forming Geistesmasse (the quality of the accompanying representation) depends on the relative form of motion of the matter in which it is formed. This is a two-way correspondence: equal forms of motion give equal forms of Geistesmasse, and conversely equal forms of Geistesmasse presuppose equal forms of motion.
(8) All simultaneously forming Geistesmassen (marginal note: in our cerebrospinal system) combine through a physical, chemical-electrical process between the places where they form.
(10) Each Geistesmasse strives to generate a like-formed one. Hence it strives to restore the form of motion of matter under which it was formed.
(11) This striving acts wherever the forming or just-formed Geistesmasse is connected with it, directly or indirectly. It is weaker the more remote the connection.

The next page completes the scheme with (12). The motion of matter at a point is determined by two things:
- the weighted striving of all connected Geistesmassen;
- the external forces depending on the position of matter.

The numbering skips 5, 6 and 9, which are taken from the parallel sheet (Blatt 12).

(B) Right column, slip from another sheet: into every ponderable atom a definite quantity of 'Stoff' flows at each instant, proportional to the gravitational force, and disappears there. That is, it ceases to act lastingly on the world of appearances. This is Riemann's known ether-sink picture of gravitation and its link to the vanishing of Geistesmassen from the phenomenal world.

Interpretation (mine, not on the page): in the published 'Gravitation und Licht' fragment, an incompressible medium flowing radially into a sink of strength Q has speed Q/(4*pi*r^2) at distance r. Proportionality of the absorbed quantity to the mass then yields an inverse-square law.

(C) The marked passage '1. Voranzustellen!' (to be put first) contains:
- The famous marginal self-characterization: the author is a Herbartian in psychology and epistemology (methodology and eidolology), but mostly cannot follow Herbart's philosophy of nature and the related metaphysical disciplines (ontology and synechology).
- An argument copied from another sheet. The assumption of a soul as a single bearer of what is permanent rests on the close connection and interpenetration of all representations. Yet such a bearer cannot explain why a new representation enters these particular connections with this particular strength; that cause must be sought in the representations themselves. Given these causes, a unitary bearer is superfluous.
errors: No mathematical errors; the page contains no calculations.
Internal numbering is non-consecutive (1,2,3,4,7,8,10,11); 5, 6 and 9 are on the parallel sheet (Blatt 12) or omitted. This is a draft artifact, not an error of reasoning.

The cross-reference '(8)' at the end of postulate 10 appears to point to the content of postulate 7 (form of motion determines form of Geistesmasse), not to postulate 8. This is a possible slip in the internal reference.

results.what: Theory of 'Geistesmassen': permanent traces of mental acts that tend to reproduce the motion-form of matter under which they arose; association strength decreases with remoteness of connection
results.modern_name: Associationist/memory-trace (engram-like) theory of reproduction; psychophysical parallelism
results.usually_credited_to: Herbart (Vorstellungsmechanik, 1820s); engram concept later by Semon (1904)

results.what: Gravitation as continuous absorption of a medium ('Stoff') into each ponderable atom, at a rate proportional to the gravitational force
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (published posthumously in Werke 1876, 'Gravitation und Licht'); similar ideas by Fatio, Le Sage, Euler and others

results.what: Self-description as Herbartian in psychology and epistemology but not in natural philosophy
Argument that a unitary soul-substance is superfluous once the causes of associations lie in the representations themselves
results.modern_name: Critique of substantial soul / bundle-type theory
results.usually_credited_to: Hume-type bundle theory; Riemann's version is printed in his philosophical fragments

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a draft of Riemann's philosophical fragments, whose content (Geistesmassen, the Herbartian self-description, ether absorption by atoms) Dedekind and Weber printed in the Werke and historians have discussed widely. It contains no mathematics.

checkable.asserts: My illustration, not on the page. The radial inflow of an incompressible medium into a point sink of strength Q is divergence-free for r>0, so the flux through every sphere is constant. This is the basis of an inverse-square law in Riemann's ether-sink picture.
Placeholder consistency check (mine): the flux 4*pi*r**2*v equals Q, independent of r.

transcription_corrections: Line 1: above 'welches sie' a word is inserted that looks more like 'stets' ('welches sie stets zu reproduciren strebt') than 'sich'; uncertain.
Postulate 4 reads 'auf's Innigste und Mannigfachste', consistent with the transcription.
Marginal note: the manuscript abbreviates 'H.'s Naturphilosophie'; 'Herbart's' is an expansion.
The reference next to '++/' may read '(S. 13)' rather than '(S. 18)'; compare the next page's '+) cf. ... S. 18'. Uncertain.
Bottom pencil note 'bis Seite 13' is faint; it may read 'bis Seite 13' or 'bis Blatt 13'.
